title: Write a Bug Report Someone Else Can Reproduce
objective: Write a bug report for a real Python defect such that a teammate who has not seen the code can reproduce it from the report alone, and attach a failing automated case that matches the reported actual result.
whyThisMatters: 'It doesn't work' is not a bug report. Numbered steps, expected versus actual, environment, and a minimal failing input are what make a ticket actionable — and what keep a teammate from bouncing it back to you.
evidence: The bug-report Markdown file containing environment, numbered steps, expected result, actual result, and a minimal input or script
A reproduction log from a second attempt (another person, or you after at least a few hours in a new terminal) that used only the report
Output of a failing automated test or script whose printed or asserted actual result matches the report's actual-result sentence
AI disclosure entry if AI helped draft the report or the failing case
acceptanceCriteria: The report file contains all of: environment (OS, Python version, relevant package versions), numbered reproduction steps, expected result, actual result, and a minimal input or script.
A second reproduction attempt is documented as succeeding from the report alone, or the log quotes the exact sentence that had to be added before it succeeded.
A committed failing test or script produces output that matches the report's actual-result sentence.
The report does not include a proposed patch or a root-cause claim presented as fact — this task is the report, not the fix.
